scenarios.name: QuickShip Delivery Analytics
scenarios.summary: QuickShip is a fictional last-mile delivery company operating in three Nigerian cities: Lagos, Abuja, and Kano. A junior data analyst is investigating delivery-time performance, exploring distributions and outliers, computing correlations between distance, package weight, and delivery time, and preparing findings for the operations manager.
glossary_example_vocab: average delivery time rose from 22 to 30 minutes

scenarios.name: QuickShip Relational Database
scenarios.summary: The relational schema behind QuickShip: customers, orders, products, and order_items tables. Used to teach entities, primary keys, foreign keys, referential integrity, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, normalization, and ER diagram reading.

assets.title: QuickShip Delivery Times — Small Sample (9 orders)
assets.description: Nine delivery-time observations used to illustrate distribution shape. Values: 18, 20, 22, 22, 26, 28, 34, 41, 52 minutes. Right-skewed: bulk sits 18–28 min, tail trails right. Mean ≈ 29.2, median = 26.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Unique order reference

columns.name: delivery_minutes
columns.description: Actual delivery time in minutes from dispatch to doorstep

variants.purpose: Outlier version: the 52-minute order is replaced with an 80-minute order and the 34/41 orders are dropped, leaving the 7-value batch from the outlier teaching block.

planted_issues.description: 80-minute delivery is extreme relative to the rest of the batch (18–28 min); could be a data-entry error (8.0 → 80) or a genuine event such as a road closure.

assets.title: QuickShip Delivery Frequency Table — 21 Orders
assets.description: Frequency table of 21 delivery times grouped into 10-minute bins (with a single 50–80 min bin matching the glossary). Bins: 10–20 min: 4 orders, 20–30 min: 9 orders (modal bin), 30–40 min: 5 orders, 40–50 min: 2 orders, 50–80 min: 0 orders, 80–90 min: 1 order. Right-skewed with a single far-out delivery past 80 minutes.

columns.name: bin_label
columns.description: 10-minute delivery-time bin label (e.g. '10–20 min')

columns.description: Lower bound of the bin (inclusive)

columns.name: bin_upper
columns.description: Upper bound of the bin (exclusive)

columns.name: order_count
columns.description: Number of orders whose delivery time falls in this bin

assets.title: QuickShip Delivery Orders — Extended (20 orders)
assets.description: Twenty delivery orders with distance, package weight, city, priority flag, and delivery time. Supports correlation analysis (distance/time ≈ 0.83 strong positive; weight/time ≈ -0.42 moderate negative; distance/weight ≈ -0.37 weak negative) and city-level comparisons (Lagos, Abuja, Kano). Priority toggle illustrates correlation-vs-causation caveat.

assets.title: QuickShip Pairwise Correlation Matrix (3 variables)
assets.description: Pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients for distance_km, package_weight_kg, and delivery_minutes. Values: distance/delivery_minutes=0.82 (strong positive), weight/delivery_minutes=-0.41 (moderate negative), distance/weight=-0.38 (weak negative). Used to teach ranking by magnitude and confounding variable reasoning.

assets.title: QuickShip City Delivery Summary — Two Months
assets.description: Monthly average delivery times and order volumes for Lagos, Abuja, and Kano across two months. Lagos average rose from 22 to 30 minutes. Supports bar chart (city comparison), line chart (trend over time), pie chart (share of total orders), and stakeholder recommendation teaching.

assets.title: QuickShip Customers Table
assets.description: The customers entity table: customer_id (primary key), name, city. Used to teach entities/tables, primary keys, entity integrity, one-to-many relationships, normalization, and foreign key referencing.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Primary key — unique integer label for each customer (not a quantity)

columns.name: name
columns.description: Customer full name

columns.name: city
columns.description: Customer's city: Lagos, Abuja, or Kano

variants.purpose: Duplicate-row variant to illustrate normalization: same customer appears twice, violating primary key uniqueness.

planted_issues.description: customer_id 1 appears twice — a duplicate row that violates the primary key uniqueness requirement and illustrates the update anomaly risk in un-normalized data.

assets.title: QuickShip Orders Table
assets.description: The orders entity table: order_id (primary key), customer_id (foreign key → customers), delivery_minutes. Used to teach foreign keys, referential integrity, one-to-many relationships, and normalization. Multiple orders per customer demonstrate the 1:M relationship.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Primary key — unique integer label for each order (not a quantity)

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Foreign key referencing customers.customer_id — identifies which customer placed this order

columns.name: delivery_minutes
columns.description: Actual delivery time in minutes

variants.purpose: Orphan-record variant: order 107 references customer_id 99 which does not exist in the customers table, illustrating a referential integrity violation.

planted_issues.description: customer_id 99 does not exist in the customers table — this order row is an orphan record that violates referential integrity.

assets.title: QuickShip Products Table
assets.description: The products entity table: product_id (primary key), name. An independent entity — a product can exist without any orders. Used to teach many-to-many relationships and junction tables. Includes the rice bag and cooking oil mentioned in teaching blocks.

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: Primary key — unique integer label for each product (not a quantity)

columns.name: name
columns.description: Product name

assets.title: QuickShip Order Items Table (Junction)
assets.description: Junction table resolving the many-to-many relationship between orders and products. Each row is one (order, product) pairing. Composite primary key: (order_id, product_id). Teaching block pairings: order 101 with rice bag (product 10), order 101 with cooking oil (product 11), order 103 with rice bag (product 10).

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Foreign key referencing orders.order_id — part of composite primary key

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: Foreign key referencing products.product_id — part of composite primary key

assets.title: QuickShip Customer Candidate Keys Table
assets.description: A customers table with four candidate columns to evaluate as primary key: customer_id (valid PK: unique, never null), name (fails: two customers share a name), phone (fails: one null), signup_date (fails: two customers signed up on the same date). Used to teach primary key selection and entity integrity.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Valid primary key candidate: unique integer, never null

columns.name: name
columns.description: Customer name — fails as PK because two customers share a name

columns.name: phone
columns.description: Phone number — fails as PK because one row has a null value

columns.name: signup_date
columns.description: Signup date — fails as PK because two customers share the same date

variants.purpose: Highlights the duplicate-name issue: customer 5 shares the name 'Amara Okafor' with customer 1, showing why name fails as a primary key.

planted_issues.description: Two customers share the name 'Amara Okafor' — name is not unique and therefore cannot serve as a primary key.

variants.purpose: Highlights the null phone issue: customer 4 has no phone number, showing why phone fails as a primary key (entity integrity requires no nulls in the PK).

planted_issues.description: Customer 4 has a null phone value — phone cannot serve as a primary key because entity integrity requires the PK to be never null.
